title: Upgrade OpenAPI generator to 7.x and its companion libraries (pre-Boot 4)
description:
## WHAT THIS IS

Upgrade the OpenAPI code generator from 6.5.0 to 7.x and bump its companion libraries,
staying on Spring Boot 3.5 (`useSpringBoot3`). This isolates the stub regeneration from the
Spring Boot 4 upgrade (gametime-c3i), which needs generator 7 for `useSpringBoot4` /
`useJackson3` — after this, that step is a flag flip.

## TRAPS & TOUCHPOINTS

- ⚠ **openapi-generator-maven-plugin** (gametime-api/pom.xml): 6.5.0 → 7.26.0 or 7.27.0
  (7.27.0 released 2026-11-02). `useSpringBoot3` defaults to true in 7.x.
- ⚠ **Regeneration changes the stubs**: expect fix-ups in `V1ApiDelegateimpl` if
  `V1ApiDelegate` signatures, imports or annotations change. gametime-api stays generated
  code only — fix in gametime-app or the spec, never by hand in gametime-api.
- ⚠ **JaCoCo excludes** (gametime-app/pom.xml) name generated classes (`ApiUtil`, `V1Api*`,
  `model/*`). Confirm 7.x doesn't emit new generated classes that land in the gate.
- **Companions** (gametime-api/pom.xml): `swagger-annotations` 2.2.28 → latest 2.2.x
  (2.2.56 at time of writing — NOT 3.0.0, springdoc 2.x expects 2.2.x);
  `jackson-databind-nullable` 0.2.7 → 0.2.13. Use whatever generator 7 expects.
- **Out of scope**: springdoc stays at 2.8.6 (it moves to 3.x with Boot 4, gametime-c3i);
  the spec stays `openapi: 3.0.0`.

## DONE WHEN

1. `mvn -f gametime-service/pom.xml clean install` succeeds on JDK 25 (unit, Cucumber, and
   the per-package JaCoCo gate).
2. CalibrationHarness (SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local,baseline, seed 1000) reproduces the
   pre-upgrade report line for line.
3. The API contract is unchanged: same endpoints and payloads, Swagger UI still serves at
   /swagger-ui.html on a local run.
close_reason: Generator 6.5.0->7.27.0, swagger-annotations 2.2.56, jackson-databind-nullable 0.2.13. clean install green (676 unit + 52 Cucumber, JaCoCo gate met); harness seed 1000 identical line for line; 17 endpoints + JSON property names unchanged; Swagger UI serves locally.

title: Upgrade project to Spring Boot 4
description:
WHAT THIS IS

Upgrade `gametime-service` from Spring Boot `3.5.14` to Spring Boot `4.x` (Spring Framework 7 / Jakarta EE 11 / Hibernate 7).

TRAPS & TOUCHPOINTS

- ⚠ **OpenAPI codegen (`gametime-api/pom.xml`)**: `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` (`6.5.0`, `<useSpringBoot3>true</useSpringBoot3>`), `jackson-databind-nullable` (`0.2.7`), and `swagger-annotations` (`2.2.28`). Verify generated delegate interfaces (`V1Api`, `V1ApiDelegate`, `V1ApiController`) compile cleanly against Spring Boot 4 / Spring WebMVC 7; bump `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` if needed.
- ⚠ **Springdoc / Swagger UI (`gametime-app/pom.xml`)**: `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` is pinned at `2.8.6` (Spring Boot 3.x) and must move to a Spring Boot 4 compatible `3.x` version so `/swagger-ui.html` and `/v3/api-docs` continue to work.
- ⚠ **Liquibase & JPA / Hibernate 7 (`ddl-auto=validate`)**: Spring Boot 4 restructures starters and upgrades Hibernate + Liquibase. Confirm the changelog (`db/changelog.yml`) and `ddl-auto=validate` pass against both H2 (tests) and Postgres (local Docker), and that Liquibase checksums on existing changesets (`1.04.1` etc.) are unaffected.
- ⚠ **Test stack (`gametime-app/pom.xml`)**: Verify `cucumber-spring` (`${cucumber.version}` = `7.14.0`) and `wiremock-standalone` (`3.13.0`) against Spring Boot 4's test context and JUnit Platform versions.
- ⚠ **SimConfig binding (`SimConfig.baseline()` & `SimConfigProfileBindingTest`)**: `SimConfig` uses Spring Boot's `Binder` and `@ConfigurationProperties` constructor binding; confirm both Spring context startup and `SimConfig.baseline()` work unchanged.

DONE WHEN

1. `gametime-service/pom.xml` parent is on Spring Boot `4.x` and all third-party pinned versions in `gametime-api/pom.xml` and `gametime-app/pom.xml` are aligned.
2. `mvn -f gametime-service/pom.xml clean install` passes all unit, integration, and Cucumber tests plus the per-package JaCoCo coverage gate.
3. The application starts cleanly against local Postgres (`spring-boot:run`) and `/swagger-ui.html` loads.
4. `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` version references are updated.
5. CalibrationHarness reproduces the pre-upgrade report line for line: capture the report on `main` **before** touching any pom (`SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local,baseline`, `-DcalibrationSeed=1000`, run from `gametime-service/`), rerun on the branch with the same seed, and diff the report block. Confirm the `Profiles:` line reads `local,baseline` in both.
design:
DECISIONS (Dave, 2026-11-17)

- D1 Spring Boot version: 4.1.2 (latest; not the 4.0.x line).
- D2 Jackson: move to Jackson 3 (Boot 4 default). Do not use the deprecated Jackson 2 compatibility module. App code only uses `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation` (GMEntity, CoachEntity), which keeps its package in Jackson 3; set the generator's `useJackson3`.
- D3 Starters: Boot 4's modular layout (`spring-boot-starter-webmvc`, per-technology starters and per-module test starters). Not `spring-boot-starter-classic`.
- D4 Liquibase: accept Liquibase 5 (5.0.4 via the Boot 4.1.2 BOM), licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (was Apache 2.0 in 4.x). Do not pin Liquibase 4.x.
- D5 Cucumber: `cucumber.version` 7.14.0 -> 7.34.9 (supports Spring 7 / JUnit 6). Not the 8.x major.
- D6 jackson-databind-nullable: remove it. Set the generator's `openApiNullable=false` and drop the dependency from gametime-api/pom.xml; the spec has no `nullable: true` fields.
notes:
MUST NOT MISS

- ⚠ `liquibase-core` alone no longer runs migrations in Boot 4 (auto-config moved to its own module). Add `spring-boot-starter-liquibase`, or a fresh DB fails `ddl-auto=validate`.
- springdoc 2.8.6 -> 3.2.0; generator gets `useSpringBoot4` (replacing `useSpringBoot3`).
- Moved test/auto-config packages are import fixes only: `AutoConfigureMockMvc`, `LocalServerPort`, `ValidationAutoConfiguration`. No `@MockBean` to migrate.
- The app serves API docs at `/api-docs` (springdoc.api-docs.path), not `/v3/api-docs` as the description says. Verify the path the app actually serves.
- Cucumber steps use `RestTemplate`; it still works in Framework 7. Moving to `RestClient` is out of scope.
close_reason: All 5 done-when criteria verified: Boot 4.1.2 parent; mvn clean install green (676 unit + 52 Cucumber, JaCoCo gate met); app started on existing local Postgres (Liquibase 5: 18 previously run, 0 run), /swagger-ui.html + /api-docs 200; CLAUDE.md/README updated; CalibrationHarness seed 1000 report identical before/after (220 lines, local,baseline).

title: Upgrade project to JDK 25
description:
WHAT THIS IS

Upgrade `gametime-service` from Java 21 to JDK 25 so the project builds and runs natively on the system default JDK (Homebrew Maven defaults to JDK 25) without a `JAVA_HOME` override.

  - `gametime-service/gametime-app/pom.xml`: `<BP_JVM_VERSION>25</BP_JVM_VERSION>` and `jacoco-maven-plugin` version
  - `.github/workflows/build.yml`: `java-version: '25'`
  - `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/todo.md`, and `.claude/skills/test-coverage/SKILL.md`: remove/update the Java 21 `JAVA_HOME` workaround notes.

DONE WHEN

1. `mvn -f gametime-service/pom.xml clean install` succeeds under JDK 25 (compilation, Lombok annotation processing, unit/integration/Cucumber tests, and the per-package JaCoCo coverage gate).
2. `CalibrationHarness` (`SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local,baseline`, seed 1000) runs cleanly on JDK 25 and reproduces the baseline report line for line (`L64X128MixRandom` determinism check).
3. `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` reflect JDK 25.

title: Guardrails: reformat the codebase to Google Java Style and gate on google_checks
description:
Bring the codebase to Google Java Style and switch the Checkstyle gate (gametime-1mj.4) from the project ruleset to google_checks.xml. Part of the quality guardrails epic.

WHY AFTER 1mj.4

1mj.4 adds Checkstyle as a lint gate on the CURRENT style (4-space indentation, some wildcard imports). This bead then moves the whole codebase to Google style in one deliberate step and points the gate at Google's ruleset.

WHAT GOOGLE STYLE CHANGES

2-space indentation, 100-column limit, no wildcard imports, a fixed import order, plus Javadoc and naming rules. Nearly every Java file changes.

APPROACH

1. Land or merge any in-flight branches first (e.g. the sim comment-pass branch), since this reformat conflicts with almost everything.
2. Run google-java-format ONCE as a one-time mechanical reformat, in its own commit. This is the only code-rewriting step; Checkstyle stays lint-only afterwards (Dave's call).
3. Fix by hand what Checkstyle still flags (Javadoc, naming, anything the formatter leaves).
4. Switch the gate to google_checks.xml. Its default severity is warning; set it to error so the build fails.
5. Add the reformat commit to .git-blame-ignore-revs.

Covers hand-written code in gametime-app (main and test). Excludes the generated gametime-api module.

DONE WHEN

- The Checkstyle gate runs google_checks.xml at error severity and mvn clean install passes with zero violations.
- A deliberate violation fails the build with a readable message (then is removed).
- Behavior is unchanged: compiled classes are identical to before the reformat, or failing that, a same-seed CalibrationHarness report (seed 1000, local,baseline) is identical line for line.
- The reformat commit is listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs.
- CLAUDE.md states the code style is Google Java Style, enforced by Checkstyle.

3. Remaining Checkstyle findings (Javadoc, naming, anything the formatter leaves) are fixed by hand in a separate commit.
4. The gate uses google_checks.xml with severity raised from warning to error, and mvn clean install passes with zero violations.
5. Behavior unchanged: compiled classes are identical before and after the reformat, or failing that, a same-seed CalibrationHarness report (seed 1000, local,baseline) is identical line for line.
6. The reformat commit is listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs.

8. Covers hand-written code in gametime-app, main and test. gametime-api (generated) is excluded.

title: Quality guardrails: static analysis, architecture rules and linting in the build
description:
WHAT THIS IS

Automated quality guardrails in the Maven build, so problems are caught the same way whether a human or an AI wrote the code. Today the only one is the JaCoCo coverage gate.

WHY

AI sessions write much of this code, and their mistakes are often quiet: a suppressed warning, a lowered threshold, a new dependency edge, a method that keeps growing. A check in the build catches those every time; a reviewer may not.

CURRENT STATE (2026-11-16)

- JaCoCo per-package gate at install; CI runs ./mvnw clean install on every push.
- No static analysis, linting, formatting or dependency checks.
- Cyclomatic complexity (JaCoCo, gametime-app): 547 methods, median 1, mean 1.75, max 18. Four methods over 10: StatsServiceImpl.getGameHighs 18, GametimeServiceImp.setLineup 17, StatsServiceImpl.rule 16, PossessionEngine.resolveReboundFoul 11.

TOOLS (children: PMD, SpotBugs, ArchUnit, Checkstyle; 5 and 6 are still undecided)

1. PMD 7: complexity (method cyclomatic complexity limit, e.g. 15), unused code, common bug patterns. A complexity limit of 15 flags 3 methods today.
2. SpotBugs: bytecode bug patterns (null handling, equals/hashCode, concurrency). Needs Lombok-generated code excluded.
3. ArchUnit tests: architecture rules as unit tests. First rule: GameSimulator must not depend on the top-level service (TeamQueryService exists to keep that edge out). Also: gametime-api stays generated-only; entities do not depend on services.
4. Checkstyle: lint only. It fails the build and never rewrites code (Dave's call: linting over auto-formatting).
5. Dependency checks: OWASP dependency-check or Dependabot for known vulnerabilities.
6. Optional: Error Prone, compile-time bug checks (works on JDK 21).

APPROACH

- Add one tool at a time, each its own commit.
- Start each in report-only mode, fix or explicitly baseline what it finds, then turn on failing the build.
- Every threshold and exclusion lives in one config file in the repo, so lowering one shows up in review.
- Java 21 only (never JDK 25), and Lombok must keep working.

DONE WHEN

- Each child's tool is in the build and fails mvn clean install, so CI fails too.
- The existing findings are fixed or deliberately baselined, each with a reason.
- CLAUDE.md lists the gates next to the JaCoCo one, so every session knows they exist.
acceptance_criteria:
EPIC
1. Children gametime-1mj.1 (PMD), .2 (SpotBugs), .3 (ArchUnit), .4 (Checkstyle) and .5 (Google style) are all closed against their own acceptance criteria.
2. CI fails on a violation from any of the tools, shown at least once per tool.
3. CLAUDE.md has one short "Guardrails" list naming every gate, its config file, and that lowering a threshold or adding a baseline needs Dave's sign-off.
4. The combined time the tools add to mvn clean install is recorded.
5. Dependency checks (OWASP or Dependabot) and Error Prone are each either given a child bead or explicitly declined, with the reason in this epic's notes.

title: Turnover floor: reroute isTurnover off PROB_FLOOR and re-tune base-turnover
description:
WHAT THIS IS

`sim.base-turnover` (0.0527) sits just above `PROB_FLOOR` (0.02), so ~40-45% of
possessions — any matchup where the ball-handler outruns the defense by more
than ~0.65 skill points — are floored at 2% and insensitive to the constant
(measured elasticity 0.17, #042 D4). Good ball-handlers facing average defense
are raised to a 2% turnover chance, compressing the low end of a turnover
leaderboard.

Take `TurnoverResolver.isTurnover` off `PROB_FLOOR` and re-tune
`sim.base-turnover`, following the same move #046 (`gametime-g1g`) made for
blocks.

TRAPS

- ⚠ `SimConfig.contestProbability()` clamps to `PROB_FLOOR` internally.
  `TurnoverResolver.isTurnover` currently wraps `contestProbability(...)` in a
  second `clampProbability(...)` after multiplying by `defensivePressure`.
  Replacing only the outer clamp leaves the inner `PROB_FLOOR` clamp intact.
  Route the contest through `rareEventProbability(..., SimConfig.SENSITIVITY)`
  (or a dedicated floor-free `SimConfig` helper like `blockProbability`) and
  clamp `defensivePressure * ...` via `clampRareProbability`.
- ⚠ Steals are derived (`turnovers * STOLEN share`, #042 I), not tuned. The nine

title: Phase 3 — Foul-out rate: engine 0.386 vs real 0.106 (needs design pass)
description:
WHAT THIS IS

The engine fouls players out about 3.6 times as often as the real NBA.
Bring it down. This is engine work and starts with a design pass.

THE NUMBERS

Per team per game. Real = ESPN box scores, every 2025-26 regular-season
game. Engine = the 5-seed baseline in docs/calibration.md.

                               Real    Engine
  Finished with 4 fouls        1.01    1.01
  Finished with 5 fouls        0.43    0.56
  Fouled out (6)               0.106   0.386

Read as a funnel:

                                          Real    Engine
  Players reaching 4 or more              1.55    1.96
  Of those, share reaching 5 or more      35%     48%
  Of players at 5, share who foul out     20%     41%

So there are two problems, and the second is the bigger one:
  1. About 26% too many players get into foul trouble at all.
  2. A player sitting on 5 fouls is twice as likely to pick up the sixth.

WHERE NOT TO LOOK (docs/calibration.md, "Foul-outs")

  - Do not lower the foul rate. Total fouls are right (19.35 vs 19.9) and
    lowering them breaks free throws and points, which are sourced.
  - Do not re-tune the foul-trouble sit curve. It is measured as saturated
    (#031).

WHERE TO LOOK

  - calibration.md's existing diagnosis: the same defenders are picked to
    commit fouls too often. That fits problem 1.
  - Problem 2 is new. Something about how a real player or coach behaves at
    5 fouls is missing from the engine. This is a reading of the numbers and
    has not been checked against the engine code. The design pass should
    confirm or reject it first.

DONE WHEN

  - A design pass has produced a decisions.md entry and an execute-ready plan.
  - After execution, a 5-seed baseline run shows the 4 / 5 / 6 rows close to
    the real ones. Judge by the three rows together, not the foul-out count
    alone.
  - Fouls, FTA, points and FGA are still on target in the same run.
  - docs/calibration.md and the harness strings are updated to match.

NOT PART OF THIS BEAD

  - Promoting foul-outs from a ballpark to a TARGET. That is Dave's call and
    can be made in the design pass.
  - Technicals and flagrants. Accepted as they are (Dave, 2026-11).
notes:
EXPERIMENTS, 2026-11-16 (ahead of the design pass)

Three experiments, each swept on the 5-seed baseline (seeds 1000-5000).
Per team per game. Baseline here reads 4/5/6 = 0.98 / 0.50 / 0.38
(calibration.md lists 1.01 / 0.56 / 0.39; the 5-foul row there looks stale).

CODE READING (confirms "problem 2" in the description)

• The foul count is read only by the rotation's sit roll. A defender on 5
fouls is drawn as often and fouls as often as on 0.
• The sit roll already uses substitutionAggressiveness (x0.82 to x1.20). At
5 fouls every coach benches within a possession or two.
• The return is foul-blind and clock-blind: the freshest bench player comes
back, whatever his fouls.
• Shooting, non-shooting and and-1 fouls all land on the one defender drawn
for the attempt. Only rebounding fouls, charges and technicals land elsewhere.

1. GENERAL WIDENING - not a lever

With some probability, redraw the committer of a rolled foul across the five
by foulProne.

  spread   4 / 5 / 6             fouls   FTA
  0        0.98 / 0.50 / 0.38    19.11   23.48
  0.25     0.97 / 0.54 / 0.38    19.41   23.86
  0.50     1.02 / 0.50 / 0.34    19.42   23.56
  0.75     0.99 / 0.49 / 0.32    19.39   23.82

Back-of-envelope (Poisson, not a harness result): fouls handed out purely by
minutes played give about 1.6 players reaching 4+ and about 0.26 foul-outs.
Real is 1.55 and 0.106. So real players reach 4 at about the chance rate and
then foul out far less than chance. No sharing rule can get below about 0.26.
calibration.md's "same defenders are picked too often" explains little.

2. CAUTION ON THE FOUL ROLL - works, but moves the totals

Multiply the foul and and-1 chance by a curve on the defender's foul count
(values at 4 / 5 fouls).

  curve         4 / 5 / 6             fouls   FTA     FGA
  0.80 / 0.60   1.06 / 0.53 / 0.27    18.92   23.08   89.94
  0.65 / 0.40   1.18 / 0.49 / 0.20    18.79   22.84   90.10
  0.50 / 0.25   1.27 / 0.48 / 0.11    18.56   22.40   90.30

Rejected by Dave: it removes fouls, so FTA, fouls and FGA come off target.

3. HANDOFF - totals hold, 4 and 5 rows get worse

The foul roll is unchanged. A drawn defender keeps his foul with the curve's
probability; otherwise one of his four teammates on the floor is charged
(drawn by foulProne). Same curve weights the rebounding-foul committer draw.

  curve                  4 / 5 / 6             fouls   FTA     FGA     pts
  0.80 / 0.60            1.10 / 0.58 / 0.28    19.22   23.66   89.52   115.5
  0.65 / 0.40            1.22 / 0.58 / 0.22    19.33   23.78   89.44   115.5
  0.50 / 0.25            1.31 / 0.59 / 0.15    19.32   23.84   89.54   115.5
  0.80@3, 0.55 / 0.25    1.21 / 0.57 / 0.15    19.47   23.94   89.34   115.8

• Points, FGA, FG%, blocks and top-slot minutes unchanged.
• Fouls +0.1 to +0.35 and FTA +0.2 to +0.45. Unverified reading: players who
would have fouled out stay on and keep fouling.
• Players reaching 4+ rise from 1.87 to about 2.0 (real 1.55), because
teammates absorb the fouls.

STILL OPEN

• Why 1.87 players reach 4 fouls against a real 1.55. No experiment reduced
it. A harness row with the full 0-6 foul distribution, next to the same count
from the ESPN box scores, would show where the engine departs.
• Not tried: a return gate (coach holds a troubled player out). Needs the
game clock, which reopens #031 C.
• Not tried: the defensive cost of playing carefully.
• Ruled out by Dave: changing who a player defends, and a matchup model.

STATE OF THE CODE

Experiment 3 is in the working tree, uncommitted: tunable
sim.foul-caution-factors (all 1.0 = today's engine, verified identical on
seed 1000), PossessionEngine.foulCommitter, the weight in
FoulResolver.pickCommitter, tests. Tunables 64. Experiments 1 and 2 were
removed. No docs updated.
OUTCOME, 2026-11-16 — the handoff is built (decisions.md #047), uncommitted

Supersedes STATE OF THE CODE above. Dave chose the handoff and accepted
foul-outs near 0.2 to protect the 4-foul row.

• Curve sim.foul-trouble-keep-probabilities = 1, 1, 1, 0.90, 0.70, 0.40, 1.
• sim.non-shooting-foul-share 0.4123 -> 0.427 to re-land FTA.
• 5-seed landing: 4 / 5 / 6 = 1.10 / 0.58 / 0.21 (was 0.98 / 0.50 / 0.38).
  Points 115.40, FGA 89.46, FTA 23.56, fouls 19.37.
• Full build and coverage gate pass. Docs, diagrams and harness string updated.

NOT DONE (why this bead stays open)

• The Done test is all three rows close to real. The 4 and 5 rows are not:
  about 1.9 players reach 4 fouls against a real 1.55, and no lever is known.
• Drift found on the way: with no engine change, today's code measures
  blocks 4.97, fouls 19.11, points 115.48 against calibration.md's 4.81,
  19.35, 115.82. Most of the table's Current column was not re-measured.
close_reason: Foul handoff landed (decisions.md #047): foul-outs 0.38 -> 0.21, totals on target. ~0.2 accepted by Dave to protect the 4-foul row. The excess of players reaching 4 fouls has no known lever and is recorded in calibration.md.

title: Source the real shooting-foul share behind sim.non-shooting-foul-share
description:
WHAT THIS IS

Find out what share of real NBA fouls are shooting fouls, and compare it to
what the engine produces.

WHY

sim.non-shooting-foul-share was never measured from real basketball. It is
simply the value that makes free-throw attempts land on 23.5 per game.

So FTA is on target, but possibly for the wrong reason. The engine could be
calling too many shooting fouls and too few bonus trips (or the reverse) and
the FTA row would look identical. This is the number that says whether the
shooting-foul composition work (#039) is right, or only consistent with
itself.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD

The other unsourced benchmarks (gametime-7gi) are lookups. This one is not
published as a single figure. docs/calibration.md says it needs to be derived
from play-by-play data, so it is more work and may stall.

DONE WHEN

The "Non-shooting-foul share" section of docs/calibration.md records:
  - the real figure
  - the named source and the season
  - how it was derived, in enough detail to repeat it
  - how it compares to the engine's realized share, from a 5-seed
    CalibrationHarness run on the baseline profile

Before comparing, check exactly what the engine's knob divides. The real
figure must be defined the same way (same numerator, same denominator), or
the comparison means nothing.

If no usable data can be found, record what was tried and leave the row
marked unsourced. That is a valid outcome.

NOT PART OF THIS BEAD

  - Do not change sim.non-shooting-foul-share or any other constant. This
    bead measures; it does not tune.
  - If the real figure and the engine disagree, propose a follow-up. Moving
    this knob also moves FTA, and it is paired with base-no-basket-foul, so a
    fix is engine work with its own design pass.

title: Engine sub-phase candidate: game initialization (10 check-ins + jump ball) + substitution events
description:
Collects the game-event work the Phase 4 design pass (gametime-ta7) uncovers. Decide at the END of that pass whether this runs before Phase 4 executes (Phase 4 then derives these facts from the log) or after (Phase 4 ships interim columns that later flip to derived).

Today: no tip-off. PossessionEngine gives HOME the first possession of every period (homeOnOffense = poss % 2 == 0, poss restarts per period), so AWAY always has the last. Substitutions emit no events.

Model (Dave, 2026-10-04): a game-initialization phase of 10 CHECK-IN events (all starters) + a JUMP BALL that decides first possession (primary = winning jumper, opponent = losing jumper, which satisfies the counterparty invariant); the possession arrow then sets periods 2-4. CHECK-OUT/CHECK-IN pairs at every substitution, including forced removals (foul-out, ejection).

Facts this would make derivable, as found so far: box_score.started (Q3), the player's team per game (Q2), plus/minus.
Open for its own design pass: new play_type(s) (closed enum, game-events.md rule 3) and the offense/defense columns on pre-tip events; the jump-ball skill (engine reads skills, not attributes); RNG stream change means seeded tests re-baseline; flow diagrams gain a branch.
notes:
box_score.started stays a column, filled at game end from the log: a CHECK_IN event with outcome = STARTER (preferred, self-describing like the FREE_THROW source outcomes), or a check-in in period 0 (works, but every reader of period must handle 0). Not the first N events, which is fragile. (gametime-ta7 Q3)
Open (from gametime-ta7 Q8): how the tip-off event relates to game.played_at. Dave's idea: tip-off event create_date = the moment the game started. Holds in Phase 4 (Postgres NOW() is transaction start, the sim is one transaction) but not from Phase 5, where played_at is game-world calendar time and create_date is real-world run time. Recommended framing: events carry no time (#024 E); the tip-off event's time IS game.played_at by definition.

title: Measure the generated player population's mean per skill against the avg-10 scale
description:
Realized FT% is `ftBase + 0.20 × (freeThrows − 10)/10` and the population's mean `freeThrows` is
~13.8, so `sim.ft-base` was pulled down to land 78%: a global constant correcting a population
effect. Other `base-*` constants may be absorbing the same bias invisibly.

Measuring is cheap and says at once whether this is one skill or systemic; fixing it is a
player-generation pass.

_Migrated from docs/backlog.md (2026-10)._
acceptance_criteria:
MEASUREMENT
1. All 23 computed skills are measured over the seeded league as the engine loads it (all 422 players, skills computed by the mappers): average, standard deviation, minimum and maximum.
2. Each skill has two averages: a roster average (every player once) and a minutes-weighted average (from the harness's simulated games). The minutes-weighted one is what a base-* constant ends up correcting for.
3. It is a permanent, report-only CalibrationHarness section with no targets, so it re-measures after every player tuning.

READING THE RESULT
4. A skill is flagged when its minutes-weighted average is more than ±1.0 from the scale average of 10 (SimConfig.SCALE_AVG).
5. Each flagged skill names the base-* or other constant the engine reads it through, the way sim.ft-base absorbs the freeThrows skew. A flagged skill the engine never reads is recorded as having no effect.
6. A one-line verdict: one skill, or systemic.
7. Results are recorded in a new docs/calibration.md section on skill population against the scale; the FT% row's note points there instead of carrying its own 13.8.
8. If systemic, a follow-up bead for a player-generation pass is PROPOSED with the exact bd create command, not created.

GUARDRAILS
9. No engine or SimConfig change: a same-seed harness run is identical to before, apart from the new section.
10. mvn clean install passes.

OUT OF SCOPE
Fixing the generator or re-tuning any base-* constant. Every constant named under 5 would move with a generator fix, so that is its own planned pass.
close_reason: Measured: report-only Skill population section in CalibrationHarness, results in calibration.md. Systemic by the min-wt rule (6-8 skills flagged) but the roster is centred (all means within 0.5 of 10); the lift is rotation/shot selection. FT per attempt 13.6 explains ft-base exactly. Same-seed main report identical; mvn clean install green.

2. The full test suite is green on Java 21 with validate on (every entity matches the Liquibase-built schema on H2).

title: Restructure resolvePossession's second-chance loop (behavior-free)
description:
Code quality only: no event, rate or calibration number changes; the payoff is the cost of adding
the next retention path. The offense keeps the ball at eight sites, each an
`offensiveRetentions++` at a different depth of one method: ordinary offensive rebound, block
recovery, OOB-offense (shares block recovery's branch), rebounding foul (offensive board off the
bonus trip's last FT), flagrant on a stopped shot, flagrant on a made shot, bonus free throws,
and shooting-foul / and-1 free throws. (#034 B; docs/engine-traps.md)

Two concrete costs: the cap is enforced two ways (five sites guard with
`if (result.offenseRetains())` with the cap pushed into the helper, three test `!capReached`
inline), so a ninth path has two precedents to copy; and threading one new variable
(`putbackCandidate`) touched six of the eight, set at five and deliberately null at the two
flagrant sites.

**Done** = one place that says "the offense kept the ball": one cap check, one
putback-candidate rule, one `continue`.

⚠ **Prove it moved nothing**: run the harness, `git stash`, run again on the **same seed**,
diff; identical line for line or the claim is false.
⚠ **Must not ride a tuning pass**: a control-flow change alongside a recalibration blurs what
moved a number.

_Migrated from docs/backlog.md (2026-10)._
close_reason: Done in 34ecc50 + follow-up. resolvePossession is a loop over resolveAttempt and five phase methods returning AttemptResult; the loop alone applies the cap, the retention counter and the putback candidate, with no continue. The cap is still an input to MissedShotResolver (missed shots and live FTs) because it shapes the board draw; moving it would change events and the RNG stream (engine-traps.md). Same-seed harness (seed 1000, local,baseline) identical line for line; mvn clean install green.

title: BoxScoreReconciler: derive box_score from game_event and diff per column
description:
Derive from `game_event` what can be derived, diff it against the persisted `box_score` rows,
report per column. Today every column is an event-time copy of an in-memory accumulator;
**nothing queries `game_event`**, so the counter and the event cannot double-count and equally
are not forced to agree. Context: docs/risks.md "Stats are written twice".

**A reconciliation, not a replacement.** The box score is the deliberate exception to
derive-don't-store (#028 A1, #023 F, #034 F); #020 settled that events are the source of truth
and the row is a denormalized snapshot. The only real failure is an *undetected* divergence. A
full rewrite yields a hybrid worse than either pure design, and re-aggregating a growing log on
every read reopens #019's pagination call.

⚠ **`minutes` is NOT derivable from any event** — a possession-share projection with no clock
(#023 A). Say so explicitly; don't skip it.
⚠ **`outcome` is free text and one value was renamed with no migration** — `COMMON_FOUL` →
`NON_SHOOTING_FOUL` (#040 M/N), so pre-§3.17 rows hold the old string. **Decide and record
which**, or the reconciler silently under-counts fouls on old games.
⚠ Rebounds must exact-match `OFFENSIVE`/`DEFENSIVE` — `OUT_OF_BOUNDS_*` rows are not rebounds
(#026 E); fouls must exclude `TECHNICAL_FOUL` (#032 E). Deriving `points` re-implements
`pointsFromEntity` — share it or cite it, don't copy it.

**Timing: Phase 4**, when season aggregation makes a drifted row compound. Subsumes #041's
`box_score.steals` follow-up. Phase 4's design pass should see this (docs/roadmap.md).

_Migrated from docs/backlog.md (2026-10)._
close_reason: Superseded by decisions.md #045 B: box_score is derived from game_event at game end and compared per column with the counters; any diff throws and rolls back (GameSimulator.verifyAgainstCounters).

title: Source four unsourced calibration benchmarks: foul-outs, technicals, flagrants, minutes
description:
WHAT THIS IS

Four numbers in docs/calibration.md are guesses. Nobody can point to where
they came from. Find the real NBA figure for each and write down the source.

  1. Foul-outs             today: ballpark ~0.1-0.25 per team per game
  2. Technicals            today: ballpark ~0.3-0.4 per team per game
  3. Flagrants             today: ballpark ~0.13-0.20 per team per game

The fifth unsourced number, the shooting-foul share, is a different kind of

WHY

The engine is judged against these rows. While they are guesses, "the engine
matches" only means it matches a number a past session wrote down.
Foul-outs is the sharpest case: the engine sits at 0.386, above the guessed
range, and we cannot say whether the engine or the range is wrong.

DONE WHEN

For each of the four, docs/calibration.md records:
  - the figure
  - the named source and the season
  - league average or per-team mean
  - pace-adjusted or not

And in the same change:
  - the "Still unsourced" line in calibration.md no longer lists them
  - any CalibrationHarness "(target ~N)" string that quotes a changed
    number is updated to match

For minutes, the two figures already in the table are enough (top-starter
average and the ceiling). A full minutes curve is out of scope.

If a figure cannot be found, say so in the row and leave it marked unsourced.
That is a valid outcome. Do not substitute a near-enough number.

NOT PART OF THIS BEAD

  - No engine change and no SimConfig change. This is a documentation chore.
  - A row does not become a TARGET just because it now has a source. It stays

title: Revisit: player team tenure as date ranges (start/end) vs. the player_team_hist journal
description:
**Revisit, not decided.** Tabled 2026-11 (Phase 4 execution): should a player's team tenure be readable as date ranges (start_date / end_date) instead of only as the move journal player_team_hist is today?

**Why it came up.** "Which team was this player on at time T?" is a simple range query against stints, and an awkward "latest move before T, unless it was a RELEASE" against the journal.

**The two shapes on the table:**
- **A view** (`player_team_stint`) deriving start/end from the journal with `LEAD(transaction_date)`. Same range queries; writes stay one appended row per move, so nothing can drift.
- **Stored columns** on player_team_hist: `start_date NOT NULL`, `end_date` nullable. Every move closes the open stint and opens a new one in one transaction (`assign()` / `removePlayerFromTeam()` in GametimeServiceImp). Gives up append-only.

**Settle before choosing:**
- ⚠ Moves are stamped in wall-clock time; games carry game-world time (`played_at`, #045 G). Ranges can't be compared to games until moves carry game-world dates — decide with Phase 5's schedule.
- ⚠ The seed roster wrote no history rows (`gametime-6x9`), so a `NOT NULL start_date` needs that fixed first.
- Box scores do NOT need this: `box_score.team_id` already stores the team per game (#045 D).

**What would make it real:** a consumer that asks "team at date" — trade deadlines, contracts, career splits by date, transaction history views.
notes: Option 3 (raised 2026-11): merge player_team into the stint table — current team = the row with end_date IS NULL. ⚠ This REOPENS #012, whose split exists for 'one team at a time': player_team's PK on player_id enforces it for free. A merged table needs a partial unique index (not in H2: a generated-column workaround), every current-roster read (TeamQueryService, lineup, roster caps, the sim squad) must filter end_date IS NULL, lineup_role / rotation_order would live on the open row only, and an end_reason column keeps RELEASE vs TRADE. Options 1–2 keep #012 intact.

title: Player plus/minus, derived from check-in/check-out events
description: Point differential while a player is on the floor. Not derivable today: substitutions emit no events. Once gametime-3sc lands (check-in/check-out events), derive at game end like the other box_score columns (Phase 4 decision A): replay the running score from made SHOT/FREE_THROW events in sequence order, and credit each player the margin over their on-floor intervals. Lands as a box_score column plus season aggregates. Surfaced by the Phase 4 design pass (gametime-ta7, Q5).

title: Historical summarization model: season-close rollups, retention, career history
description: When a season closes (Phase 5), freeze per-player and per-team season totals into summary tables that become the record for that season, which would let old seasons' game_event (~500k rows/season) and box_score rows be pruned. Phase 4 (gametime-ta7) computes live from box_score and needs neither; this is a retention decision, not a performance fix. The rollup groups by season, player and team, so it depends on box_score recording each game's team_id (Phase 4 Q2).
notes:
Scope widened (gametime-ta7 Q6): this is the design + documentation of gametime's historical model, not just the rollup tables. Settled in Phase 4: the OPEN season is always computed live from box_score; CLOSED seasons are frozen into summaries that become their record; the rollup reuses Phase 4's aggregation code and groups by (season, player, team), with team from box_score.team_id (Q2). Open for its own design pass: whether it is part of Phase 5 or its own phase (roadmap seam between season close and off-season), what is retained or pruned (game_event ~500k rows/season), career totals and records, and where the model is documented.
Open question (Phase 4 execution, 2026-11): if game_event outlives box_score for closed seasons, events need the primary player's team (game_event.primary_team_id) — otherwise old events cannot say which team a player was on (player_team is current-only, cf. #045 D). The opponent's team needs no column: it is always the other side (#041 A). Decide with retention; add before release, since it cannot be backfilled.
If primary_team_id is added: BoxScoreSummarizer credits team points by it (free throws are why — a FREE_THROW row's offense/defense does not give the shooter's team, so today GameSimulator sums by squad), and the #045 B guard asserts it equals each player's squad team / box_score.team_id. Season stats still read box_score only (#045 C).

title: Foul-outs: defender-selection over-dispersion (root cause per calibration.md)

title: Generate a constants-reference table from source
description:
Generate `docs/constants.md` from source, so docs can link to one page instead of restating values. The §3.12 pass had to update one changed multiplier in **five places**. Left out of §3.15 on purpose (#035 H).

**Re-scope, measured 2026-11-17.** Since this bead was filed, #035 A made `application-baseline.properties` the only copy of the 64 tunables, and #035 F's effective-config dump covers the runtime view. As a result, current tunable values are now rarely restated by hand:
- Most value mentions in docs are **history** (`decisions.md` "0.0527 → 0.062", measurement tables in `engine-traps.md`). History is never retro-edited, so it is not drift.
- What is still restated is mostly **statics**: e.g. `PROB_FLOOR 0.02` appears in `possession-flow-model.md`, `calibration.md` and `risks.md`.
- There is no single page listing every constant with its value and its kind (tunable or static). The reason to build this now is to have that page, not to fix active drift.

**Out of scope:** rewriting existing docs to link to the page instead of restating values. That's a follow-up once the page exists.

*Migrated from docs/backlog.md (2026-10).*
design:
**Decided 2026-11-17 (Dave):** the generator is a **separate Maven module**, `gametime-service/gametime-tools`, that you run on demand to create or update the doc.
**Decided 2026-11-17 (Dave):** the module also has a check-only test, so a stale doc **fails `mvn install`**.

**Output: `docs/constants.md`**, generated, never hand-edited.

**Sources read by the generator:**
- `SimConfig.java`: statics (`public static final`) and tunable fields, plus their bean-validation bounds.
- `application-baseline.properties`: tunable values, and the `# --- Section ---` headers used for grouping.
- `application-nineties.properties`: era deltas.

**File layout:**
1. **Banner**: "GENERATED: do not edit", the source files, the regenerate command, and the counts (`64 tunables / 29 statics`).
2. **Tunables**: one table per properties-file section, in file order. Columns:
   `key` (`sim.base-three`) · `accessor` (`baseThree()`) · `type` · `baseline` · `nineties` (blank unless overridden) · `bounds` (from `@DecimalMin`/`@DecimalMax`/`@Positive`/`@Min`).
3. **Statics**: one table per `// --- Section ---` comment in `SimConfig.java`, in source order. Columns:
   `name` · `type` · `value` · `source` (a link to its line in `SimConfig.java`).
4. **Profiles**: one line per era profile, giving how many keys it overrides.

Values are printed exactly as written in the source, not reformatted (`0.3375`, not `0.34`).

**Mechanism:**
- **New module** `gametime-tools`, added to the parent pom's `<modules>`. It has **no dependency on `gametime-app`**: it parses the three source files as text (JavaParser or line-based). That's required anyway, because reflection can't see the `// --- Section ---` comments or the literals exactly as written. It also avoids depending on the Spring Boot repackaged jar.
- **Generate** (main class `ConstantsReferenceGenerator`, run via `exec-maven-plugin`), from the repo root:
  `mvn -f gametime-service/pom.xml -pl gametime-tools compile exec:java`
  This writes `docs/constants.md`. Paths are resolved relative to the repo root, not the module directory.
- **Check:** a JUnit test in the module renders the doc in memory and compares it with the committed file. It runs in every `mvn test`/`install`, and a mismatch fails with the generate command in the message.
- **JaCoCo:** the gate is configured only in `gametime-app/pom.xml`, so this module is ungated. It still ships with tests for its parser and renderer.
- Rows are in source order, so output is deterministic.

**Where "how to regenerate" gets documented (in the same change that builds it):**
- `README.md`, **Quick start**: the generate command, with one line saying when to run it (a stale doc fails the build).
- `CLAUDE.md`, **Code conventions**: one line saying that changing a `SimConfig` constant or a `sim.*` property means regenerating `docs/constants.md`, or `mvn install` fails.
- `CLAUDE.md`, **Where things live**: add `constants.md` to the `docs/` tree, and `gametime-tools/` to the `gametime-service/` tree.
- The banner of `docs/constants.md` itself.
acceptance_criteria:
The deliverable is `docs/constants.md`. Done when:
1. `docs/constants.md` exists and follows the layout in Design: banner, tunables tables by section, statics tables by section, profiles.
2. It has exactly 64 tunable rows and 29 static rows, and the banner counts match `SimConfigProfileBindingTest.EXPECTED_TUNABLE`.
3. Every baseline value, nineties value and static value matches its source file exactly as written. The nineties column is filled only for keys that `application-nineties.properties` overrides.
4. Regenerating on an unchanged tree produces a byte-identical file (no diff).
5. The generator lives in a separate `gametime-tools` module with no dependency on `gametime-app`, and the documented command regenerates the file from the repo root.
6. Changing any constant without regenerating makes `mvn install` fail, and the failure message names the generate command.
7. The generate command is documented in `README.md` (Quick start) and `CLAUDE.md` (Code conventions, plus the `docs/` tree), as listed in Design.

title: Player efficiency rating (PER)
description: Hollinger PER: needs league-average pace and league-wide rates per scope, normalized to a league average of 15. Computable from box_score + game.home/away_possessions once Phase 4 lands; meaningful once Phase 5 defines seasons. Left out of Phase 4 (gametime-ta7, Q5) because nothing consumes it. Simpler box-score-only alternatives if a single number is wanted sooner: Game Score, NBA EFF.

title: Idea: split PERIMETER by distance (long 2 vs short/mid jumper)
description:
Every 2-point jumper is one PERIMETER shot today: one base-perimeter, one perimeter skill, one block base, no notion of distance. A long 2, a 12-foot pull-up and a short paint jumper or floater are identical.

Why it would matter: the shot modern offenses actually cut is the LONG 2 (worth nearly a three's effort for two points). The coach shotMixLean trades mid-range for threes as one block, so a smart offense cannot drop long 2s while keeping good short jumpers. It also erases player differences: a floater specialist and a long-2 shooter are the same if their perimeter rating matches. Aggregate cost is small, since real jumper percentages sit close together in the 40s; the big rim-vs-jumper gap is already modelled by DRIVE/POST vs PERIMETER.

Cost if built: a new ShotType constant, new SHOT outcomes (game-events.md), the shot diagram, a share/base/block-base tunable each (all four tunable-count sites), a recalibration, and a shifted RNG stream that re-baselines every seeded sim test. An engine sub-phase, not a tweak.

What would make it real: a consumer that needs the split, such as a shot chart in Phase 7 play-by-play, or a coach analytics axis that targets long 2s specifically. Measure first with the per-shot-type FG% instrument.

title: Idea: the charge drawer as a counterparty
description:
A charge has a real second participant, the defender who drew it, and they would be a natural
`opponent_player_id`. The engine never picks them, so the column is deliberately null on both of
the charge's events. Picking one needs a new RNG draw, which shifts the stream and re-baselines
every seeded sim test, for a participant nothing consumes.

**What would make it real:** a consumer, such as a "charges drawn" stat or a pass that wants the
drawer's `acumen` to bend the charge rate. Then it is one draw, one existing column and one
deliberate re-baselining.

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: DOUBLE_DRIBBLE as a tenth turnover cause
description:
A real, common live-ball turnover that isn't among the nine causes. Structurally free: one enum
constant, one weight, and the outcome rides the existing `TURNOVER` event as free text. Not
numerically free: cause weights re-partition a frozen turnover count, so a tenth cause takes
share from the nine, possibly from `STOLEN`, moving the steal rate.

**What would make it real:** a pass that already owns rate movement and can absorb the
re-partition in one place.

title: Idea: a rim-protection era profile
description:
Dial blocks up to about 5.5 as a stylistic delta over `baseline`, like the parked 1990s and
three-heavy profiles. **Do not do it by moving baseline**, which is tuned to sourced targets.

Two traps: a block does **not** reduce FGA (the attempt is charged before the block fork, so a
block moves FG% and 2P%, not attempts), and `base-block-three` is inert because `PROB_FLOOR`
floors it. More blocked threes must route through `clampRareProbability` first.

Values-only once the floor question (the PROB_FLOOR audit chore) is settled.

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: talent spread as a profile axis
description:
A base rate says where the league sits; a sensitivity says how far apart players within it are
(`probability = base + SENSITIVITY × (skillA − skillB)/10`). Low compresses the league (roster
quality hardly matters), high stretches it (stars separate). A "superteam era" vs "parity era" is
real, and this is the only lever that expresses it. Today the spread is spread across about 15
`*_SENSITIVITY` constants.

**Why not just profile them:** turning one in isolation breaks it. The block sensitivity is
deliberately small so blocks stay base-dominant, and the thin-base rare events need gentle slopes
too.

**What would make it real:** a design pass treating spread as one knob, most plausibly a single
multiplier across the family that preserves the established ratios. It needs its own
calibration, since it moves every rare-event rate at once.

title: Idea: raise the offensive-retention cap from 3 to 5
description:
`sim.max-offensive-retentions-per-possession` bounds the second-chance loop. A genuine scramble
can run longer than three retentions, and a hard wall makes that impossible rather than unlikely.

**The first step is a measurement, not a tune:** nobody has measured how often the cap binds.
Instrument how often `capReached` is true and how the retention count is distributed. If it
binds rarely, the realism gain is invisible and the aggregate cost lands on every game, so the
idea dies cheaply. If it binds often, the cap is doing calibration work and raising it is a
bigger change than this entry assumes.

**Why parked:** the cap fires on the common path across every retention channel, so raising it
adds offensive rebounds, attempts and points to every game. FGA and offensive rebounds already
sit at or past target and have no clean buy-back; see docs/calibration.md. A profile setting the
cap does not unpark this, but raising the shipped default needs a calibration pass.

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: fights and altercations
description:
Technicals and flagrants exist; fights need a temperament trigger that doesn't. The engine consumes
skills, not attributes, and `foulProne` already carries the aggression and composure composite. A
dedicated temperament axis is the open alternative, but it would be an attribute with no
consumer yet. The value is play-by-play texture, not aggregate fidelity.

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: coach competence in rotation decisions
description:
The rotation reads only `rotationDepth` and `substitutionAggressiveness`, both style axes. There
is no coach quality axis. It needs two things: a new `Coach` attribute (schema, `coach.csv`,
`EntityMapper`, landing with its consumer) and a definition of what a *better* substitution is
mechanically, since the model has no quality dimension to improve.

**Natural home:** Phase 6 (coach progression and hiring).

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: a game clock, or at least score-and-time awareness
description:
Time exists only as a possession count: shot-clock violations are a weighted draw, minutes are a
possession-share projection, and overtime is "some more turns". Downstream of that:
- no endgame (no intentional fouling, two-for-one or holding for the last shot); the last
  possession of a close game is simulated like the first
- the `clutch` skill is inert, because there is no "late and close" to key off
- no score awareness: a team down 20 and up 20 play identically
- pace cannot be a strategy

A real clock is a new axis, not a feature: a possession gains a duration, possessions stop being
interchangeable, and possession count becomes a result, which moves every per-possession rate.
**Most of the value is in awareness alone**: a possession that knows period, possessions
remaining and margin lights up `clutch`, intentional fouling and late-game shot selection
without variable-length possessions. Price the two halves separately.

**What would make it real:** a user-facing consumer, such as a timestamped play-by-play or a
late-game narrative (Phase 7 is the closest).

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: strategic substitutions
description:
The engine substitutes for fatigue, foul trouble and forced removal. Missing: matchup or going
small, hot hand, closing lineup and garbage time, score-aware rotation. They share one missing
prerequisite: the rotation step has no game-situation awareness (it isn't passed the period,
let alone the margin). The starting five also never change composition by choice; the coach
swaps individuals out of a fixed lineup but never picks a lineup.

**If promoted:** extend the foul-trouble sub's template (probabilistic, coach-scaled,
player-value-weighted) rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.

**What would make it real:** the game-situation plumbing (see the game-clock / awareness idea),
which a design pass should start with.

_Migrated from docs/ideas.md (2026-10)._

title: Idea: Offense Opportunity Event (good defense creating offense)
description:
A defensive play doesn't produce offense when it should. Today a steal or turnover just hands the
other team a normal half-court possession, but it might have been a fast break. An event for "a
defensive play creates an offensive opportunity" would be a way to reward good defenses.

**Related gap:** possessions strictly alternate, so each team's possession count is fixed by
config before tip-off. Defense improves *how well* a possession goes, never *how many* there
are, and in real basketball a live-ball steal is worth more partly because of what it leads to.

**What would make it real:** a transition play type, or letting possession count vary (pace as
an outcome). Either is a large change that moves attempts, and attempts have no spare
calibration lever (see docs/engine-traps.md).
